title: Introduce granular ramp scheduler with quantization hysteresis and tenant unit-econ gates
author: Daniela Ruiz
description: Motivation: Tenants with volatile traffic patterns need a gradual, reversible mechanism to ramp batching/cache aggressiveness and quantization profiles tied to explicit unit-economics thresholds. Current defaults apply static heuristics that either waste tokens or cause quality regressions during bursty periods. This PR adds a Granular Ramp Scheduler that drives gradual changes to batch size, prefix cache retention, and quantization tier using hysteresis windows to avoid flip-flopping. Design summary: 1) A tenant-scoped scheduler evaluates per-tenant unit-econ signals (cost per token, cold start penalty, error/regression estimator) and computes a ramp score in [0,1]. 2) Ramp score maps to a compact policy that adjusts three knobs: target batch_shape, prefix_cache_ttl, and quant_profile (fp16 -> int8/ggml variants). 3) Hysteresis is implemented as a two-window gate: an upper window to open an upgrade and a lower window to accept downgrade, plus a minimum hold-time to prevent thrash. 4) A CLI dry-run and a simulation mode are added so operators and tenant-owners can preview projected unit-cost delta and impact on latency/quality. 5) Telemetry: a new telemetry namespace (economics.ramp_scheduler) emits decisions, contributing signals, and delta estimates for SLO and cost. Implementation highlights: - scheduler/engine: added scheduler/ramp_scheduler.go (stateless worker with deterministic scoring and TTL cache of recent metrics) and scheduler/quant_hysteresis.go (hysteresis math and hold-time manager). - policy descriptors: added proto defs scheduler/policies.proto and JSON policy templates under conf/ramp_presets/*.json. - CLI: rampctl subcommands (dry-run, simulate, apply, abort) implemented in tools/rampctl to let SRE or tenant admins evaluate rules. - Telemetry: metrics and structured events added in observability/metrics/econ_ramp.go; lightweight events are emitted as JSON to the event stream to avoid cardinality explosion. - Tests: integration tests in test/integration/ramp_scheduler_test.go with synthetic workload traces and a unit-econ mock server. Backwards compatibility: defaults are conservative. If no tenant policy exists the scheduler is a no-op. Quant profile changes always pass through a safety gate that enforces quality regression thresholds from eval harness before full rollout. Migration/rollout plan: - Feature gated behind runtime.feature.ramp_scheduler (default off for existing tenants) - Stage 1 (canary): enable for 5 internal tenants with logging only and dry-run metrics for 48 hours. - Stage 2 (controlled rollout): enable aggressive ramps for opt-in tenants and expose rampctl to tenant owners. - Stage 3 (opt-in GA): enable default conservative ramps for new tenants and opt-in for existing tenants. Observability & guardrails: - Dashboards: new dashboard tile for decision rate, average ramp score, and unit-cost delta per tenant. - Alerts: misbehaving tenants (rapid thrash, repeated quality regression near quantization boundary) create an alert under SRE runbook E-CON. - Automatic rollback: if quality regressions exceed thresholds the scheduler automatically reverts quant_profile and reduces batch targets. Testing and CI: initial CI run observed a flaky e2e due to synthetic trace timeouts; increased timeouts and added deterministic seeding. All CI tests pass on final run. Related work: complements cost-playbook and tenant-warmstart components; replaces ad-hoc tenant scripts used in several SRE responses. Impact: expected median token cost reduction of 8-15% for long-tail tenants and 2-6% for bursty tenants while keeping 99th percentile latency within 10% of baseline. Known limitations: aggressive quantization is gated by evals; some extremely latency-sensitive LLM routes must opt-out. See release_notes for more details and operator steps.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can you explain how we quantify quality regression when switching quant profiles? Suggest adding a fallback to previous profile if eval score delta > 0.05.

Daniela Ruiz: Added a safety gate that compares a lightweight eval delta metric (BLEU-like proxy) and rejects promotions exceeding configured tolerance; documented fallback in docs/runbooks/econ_ramp.md.
Maya Chen: Telemetry looks high-cardinality; can we aggregate per-tenant and emit sampling?
Daniela Ruiz: Telemetry now emits aggregated rollups per minute and sampled detailed events for 1% of decisions. Reduced cardinality fields and moved large payloads to storage with event references.
Liam O'Connor: Unit tests look good. One nit: prefer context-aware timeouts in the scheduler worker.
Daniela Ruiz: Updated worker to use context with deadline and added tests for cancellation paths.
CI: initial pipeline failed on TestRampIntegration (timeout). Build retriggered and passed.
ci_log_summary: CI run #1: build passed, unit tests passed, integration TestRampIntegration timed out (flaky synthetic trace)
CI run #2: timeouts increased; all tests passed; coverage for scheduler package at 87%
E2E smoke: passed on canary environment (internal tenants)
release_notes: Introduce tenant ramp scheduler: conservative defaults disabled by default; opt-in via runtime.feature.ramp_scheduler. Adds rampctl for dry-run/simulation, telemetry under economics.ramp_scheduler, and safeguards for quant promotion. Expected cost savings for eligible tenants. Operators: follow docs/runbooks/econ_ramp.md to enable and monitor.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag per-tenant using deploy/feature_flags.yaml or via admin API
Run tools/rampctl simulate --tenant=<id> to preview projected cost/latency delta
Monitor dashboards: Observability > Economics > Ramp Scheduler
If quality regressions observed, run rampctl abort --tenant=<id> to immediately revert changes
